haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized before any Redis call. No counter is read or changed.
haiku-low.q2: The limit is per customer, and all of a customer's keys share one budget. Standard is 100 per minute, so about 100 total, though up to about twice that across a minute boundary.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After in seconds. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A denied request is not incremented, so it uses none of the customer's budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The request is counted when it passes the check, before forwarding, so the budget is still used.
haiku-low.q6: The gateway forwards the request anyway, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and omits X-RateLimit headers. There is no retry.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise has no number yet; it is an open decision for Product.
haiku-low.q8: Shared Redis counters keyed rl/customerId/windowStart. Each key expires 61 seconds after its first increment, which deletes old windows automatically.
haiku-low.q9: The budget resets at the start of each whole minute, since the window is fixed one minute. There is no gradual recovery.
haiku-low.q10: The check and increment run in one Lua script, which Redis executes as a single step without interleaving other commands.
haiku-low.q11: Retry-After is the seconds until the current window ends, computed from Redis TIME as 60 minus (now mod 60), giving 1 to 60.
haiku-low.q12: No retry. The request is forwarded, and the client gets only the backend response with no X-RateLimit headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized; no counter is read or written.
sonnet.q2: Limit is per customer, not per key, so all three keys share one budget (the plan's limit, e.g. 100 per minute for Standard).
sonnet.q3: A 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (seconds); the backend never sees it (not forwarded). (Whether 429 carries X-RateLimit headers is an open decision, recommended yes.)
sonnet.q4: No. A denied request is not counted; the script increments only when under the limit.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The request is counted at check time before forwarding, so a backend 500 still uses budget.
sonnet.q6: It fails open: the gateway forwards the request to the backend (no retry), emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and omits X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard = 100 per minute. Enterprise = NOT DECIDED (open decision; no number set).
sonnet.q8: In a shared Redis (primary with replica), under key rl/<customerId>/<windowStart>. Old counts are removed by a TTL: the key expires 61 seconds after its first increment.
sonnet.q9: The fixed window resets at the start of every whole minute (new window key); old keys also expire via TTL.
sonnet.q10: The check and increment run in one Lua script on shared Redis, which runs the whole script without interleaving other commands, so only one can take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Seconds until the current window ends, computed from Redis's own clock (TIME) as window - (now % window); always a whole number from 1 to 60.
sonnet.q12: No retry; the 50 ms deadline covers the whole store call. The client gets the backend response with no X-RateLimit headers.
